name: Dye-free coloured fibre
subtitle: fabric coloured by glass instead of dye

effects.effect: crushed glass in a clear material lets through only the colour where both bend light equally

effect: crushed glass in a clear material lets through only the colour where both bend light equally
how: Dyeing cloth is one of the worst water polluters on Earth and dyes fade. These fibres hold glass powder in a clear plastic that bends light exactly like the glass at just one colour (Christiansen effect); that colour passes straight through and is lost while the rest scatters back, so the cloth shows a colour set only by the choice of glass and plastic, with nothing to wash out.
obstacle: The colours come out pale and shift as the fabric warms, far from the deep shades buyers want.
why: Colour built into the fibre needs no dyeing, ending a major source of river pollution.
real: US patent 9988517 'Physical colorants for plastics based on the Christiansen effect' proposes glass-particle/polymer index-matched colorants; no Christiansen-coloured textile fibre found.
